frequency_question: How often do joint resolutions of disapproval successfully pass both chambers and survive or override a presidential veto to block a major executive nuclear or arms agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal notifications of 123 agreements or major foreign military sales submitted for congressional review where a resolution of disapproval was formally introduced and brought to a vote. Excludes informal consultations or resolutions that failed to clear committee.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 7 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 7 major historical instances where Congress attempted to use statutory disapproval mechanisms on high-stakes Middle East defense/nuclear agreements.
known_gaps: Minor arms sale notifications that were withdrawn informally by the executive before a vote are excluded as they did not reach the threshold of structural congressional blockage.
skeleton: Legislative challenges to executive foreign-policy and nuclear agreements via joint resolution of disapproval across modern statutory history.
multiplier: 0 hits out of 7 major contested legislative challenges surviving presidential vetoes or veto-proof majorities.
validity_reason: The structural bicameralism, presentment, and veto override thresholds defined by the U.S. Constitution and the Atomic Energy Act remain legally constant.
